entries.subject: Scheme interpreter
entries.object: used instead of a Common Lisp one because Scheme is simpler

spans.text: A Scheme interpreter is used instead of a Common Lisp one because Scheme is simpler, and also because Scheme is an important language that is worth knowing about.
Scheme is the only dialect of Lisp besides Common Lisp that is currently flourishing.
It is interesting that among all the programming languages in the world, Scheme is one of the smallest, while Common Lisp is one of the largest.

spans.text: Scheme has fewer built-in functions and special forms.
